targetText: the war of 1914-18 was imperialist (that is, an annexationist, predatory war of plunder) on the part of both sides
summary: World War I was not a war of self-defense or democracy for either side: it was a violent struggle between rival capitalist empires fighting over colonies, trade routes, and foreign markets.
context: Lenin dismantles war propaganda from both the Allies (Britain, France, US) and Central Powers (Germany, Austria-Hungary), demonstrating that both sides fought to expand corporate dominance and secure foreign plunder.

targetText: Capitalism has grown into a world system of colonial oppression and of the financial strangulation
summary: Capitalism evolved from local factory competition into a global web where a few wealthy nations use loans, debts, and corporations to control and drain the developing world.
context: Lenin shows how financial power replaces direct military conquest. Modern debt structures (like predatory loans to developing nations) allow rich countries to extract wealth without needing traditional colonial governors.

targetText: bribe the labour leaders and the upper stratum of the labour aristocracy.
summary: Capitalists use extra profits (superprofits) extracted from poor nations to pay higher wages and benefits to a privileged tier of workers at home, buying their political loyalty.
context: This explains why many union leaders and well-paid workers in wealthy nations backed their own governments during World War I instead of uniting with workers globally. Lenin calls this bribed group the 'labour aristocracy'.
